la:verb:suggero.gloss: to carry, bring, put or lay under
senses: to carry, bring, put or lay under

la:verb:suggero.html:
sug-gĕro (subg-), gessi, gestum, 3, v. a.,
to carry, bring, put or lay under, etc. (class., esp. in the trop. sense).
Lit.: flammam costis aëni,: ignem fornace succensā,. —
To heap up, raise, erect, build: humo, cf.: celsis suggesta theatra columnis,.—
To furnish, afford, supply ( = praebeo, suppedito, ministro): cur tu his rebus sumptum suggeris?: tela mihi,: omnium rerum apparatus, Auct. B. Alex. 3, 1: cibum animalibus,: divitias alimentaque (tellus),: feras silvae affatim suggerunt,: ructanti pinnas rubentes,. —Absol.: aliae (apes) struunt, aliae suggerunt,.—
Trop., to afford, furnish, supply: invidiae flammam ac materiam criminibus suis suggerere,: suggeram quae vendatis,: materiam interrogationi,. —
To excite, produce: sincipitamenta porcina, quae anteposita in mensā mihi bulimum suggerant, Ritschl (MSS. milvina; cf. Brix ad loc.): aut Druso ludus est suggerendus aut, etc.,is to be put upon, imposed upon,. —
To suggest, advise, prompt, offer, bring to mind: quoties aequitas restitutionem suggerit,; cf.: quae (res) suggerit, ut Italicarum rerum esse credantur eae res,reminds, admonishes,: quaedam de republicā,. — Absol.: suggerente conjuge,at the instigation of,; cf.: suggerente irā,.—
To assign, add, subjoin: huic incredibili

sententiae ratiunculas suggerit, : copiam argumentorum singulis generibus,: firmamenta causae,: verba, quae desunt,: apud quosdam veteres auctores non invenio Lucretium consulem; Bruto statim Horatium suggerunt,place next in order,; : ut quidam annales nihil praeter nomina consulum suggerant,: suggerebantur damna aleatoria,were added,.

A hint, intimation, suggestion (late Lat.), ; ; ; .

la:noun:suggestus.gloss: an elevated place made of materials poured out; raised place, height, elevation
senses: an elevated place made of materials poured out; raised place, height, elevation
a platform, dais, stage, tribune, pulpit
the higher part of a stage
la:noun:suggestus.html:
suggestus (subg-), ūs, m., and suggestum, i, n.
suggero
.
(Acc. to suggero, I.) An elevated place made of materials poured out; hence, a raised place, a height, elevation (cf. pulpitum).
Lit.
In gen.: labrum in suggestu inter dolia positum,: lapideus,: insulae,: suggestus in orchestrā,a raised seat,; Duk.; cf. : comae,i. e. a lofty head-dress,: montium,.—
In partic., a raised place to speak from to the people, to the troops, etc., a platform, stage, tribune (the class. signif. of the word): suggestum in foro exstructum adornari placuit,: C. Maenius in suggestu rostra, devictis Antiatibus, fixerat,: hac re pro suggestu pronuntiatā,; so in a milit. sense: de suggestu inquit, Auct. B. Afr. 54, 2: praemia pro suggestu tribuit,: in suggestu, in quo Galbae statua fuerat,: non in modum contionis, aut suggestu locutus,; of the prætor's tribunal: in excelso suggestu,: altior,; of the emperor's seat: in curiā,; cf.: in orchestrā,; .—
Trop., height: neve se de tanto fortunarum suggestu pessum deiciat,.—
A providing, preparation (post-class. and very rare): Circensium,: honorum,.—*
(Acc. to suggero, II.) A hint, intimation, suggestion (syn. suggestio): si ex suggestu eorum praeses dederit,.

senses: platform, stage, tribune for a speaker

suggestum, i, n.
id.

Esp., a platform, stage, tribune for a speaker: cum in communibus suggestis consistere non auderet,: illud suggestum, in quo causam dixerat, ascendens,.
